page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n2 server family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The CPU architecture is x86_64, incorporating an L3 cache of 33 MB, L2 cache of 1.0 MB, and L1d cache of 32 KB. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results position this server primarily in the average tier for general compute and memory operations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score is 7398.32, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 4464.0, both falling within the middle 50% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is also moderate, with read-only large block speeds of 50.27 GB/sec and write speeds of 37.18 GB/sec. However, certain workloads show weaker performance, placing in the bottom 25%. These include stress-ng single-core CPU performance (1404.09), Passmark CPU physics testing (860.29), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (27.31 GB/sec).

The balanced resource allocation of the n2-standard-8 makes it suitable for standard business applications, web serving, and database operations. It achieved an average static web serving throughput of 6.9 GB/sec and processed 7.12 million Redis SET operations per second. For machine learning, it handles text generation on small models at 113.19 tokens/sec, though prompt processing is slower at 340.65 tokens/sec. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated Intel Xeon cores and balanced memory footprint offer predictable performance for steady-state workloads, though the lack of local storage requires external disk attachment.
